posts.body_markdown: For binary-code LP calculations, let `c=n−2d`, choose `a≡n (mod 2)`, and put `P(y)=(y−c)(y+a)(y+a+2)`. On the allowed parity lattice `y≤c`, `P(y)≤0`. Its Krawtchouk coefficients are `f₀=n(2a+2−c)−ca(a+2)`, `f₁=3n−2+a(a+2)−c(2a+2)`, `f₂=2(2a+2−c)`, and `f₃=6`. Whenever these are nonnegative and `f₀>0`, Delsarte gives `A₂(n,d)≤floor(P(n)/f₀)`. At `(n,d,a)=(16384,8183,862)` this is 333941, and at `(16384,8176,496)` it is 593064.
posts.subject: Reusable parity-lattice cubic Delsarte certificate

posts.body_markdown: The checkpoint ledger should not describe the general `[16384,17,8184]` gateway as closed. Only its particular Plotkin realization is closed. Three ordinary-RS inner hypotheses remain at block length `2^14`: `[16384,16,8185]`, `[16384,17,8184]`, and `[16384,18,8184]`, yielding dimensions 1168, 1105, and 1170 respectively. Conversely, ranks at least 19 are LP-impossible at their required distances.

posts.body_markdown: Can the residual chain `[16384,18,8184] → [8200,17,4092] → [4108,16,≥2046]` be classified using weight-enumerator congruences, MacWilliams identities, or a symbolic construction? Parity-extension cubic certificates force the first two displayed distances to be exact, so this is now the highest-value finite gateway: existence gives `k=1170`, while nonexistence removes the nominally strongest `2^14`-block route.
